cells.quote: We found a moderate, positive, and statistically significant mean effect of 𝑔̅ = 0.11, 95% CI[0.035, 0.184] of collaborative instruction compared to single-taught controls, using the correlated-hierarchical effects (CHE-RVE) model.
cells.note: Pooled meta-analysis of 76 studies and 280 short-term effect sizes; included randomized, quasi-experimental, and observational treatment-control studies.

D.comparison: collaborative instruction involving assistants without teaching qualifications

cells.quote: From moderator analyses, we found that collaborative instruction yields effects of mostly the same size, whether the interventions involved trained teachers or assistants with no teaching qualifications.
cells.note: The study reports no exact subgroup effect sizes, significance test, or power information for this moderator comparison.

D.treatment: modern physics, quantum mechanics, and quantum computing textbooks

O.outcome_detail: extent and depth of coverage of quantum-sensing-related keywords

cells.quote: Our results show that there is significant variation in how different subjects address these concepts, both in the nature of the content covered and the depth of coverage.
cells.note: Observational textbook content analysis; no instructional treatment or learner outcome was studied.

O.outcome_detail: coverage and contexts of sensing-related keywords, including superposition and entanglement

cells.quote: We also observe notable differences in how spin-first and position-first textbooks discuss these keywords, particularly in the coverage and contexts in which core concepts such as superposition and entanglement appear.
cells.note: The comparison is between textbook approaches, not randomly assigned instructional conditions.

D.comparison: other quantum-related courses in the database

cells.quote: Together, these analyses of textbook content and course descriptions inform the quantum information science and engineering education community about potential opportunities to integrate quantum sensing topics into quantum-related courses in physics and adjacent disciplines.
